records.text: During a procedure, a cancellation was noted when the EnSite X field frame was not being recognized by the system after connecting it. Disconnecting and reconnecting the field frame as well as restarting the EnSite X amplifier resolved the issue. It was also noted that after connecting the catheters to the amplifier, there was an "amplifier error, cannot communicate with amplifier" message and the catheters were repeated shown connected and then disconnected. Trying the catheters on different ports and restarting the EnSite X system di not resolve the issue and the catheters would only show up for a few seconds on the EnSite. Mapping was not possible and when ending the study, an "unexpected error" popup was shown. Resuming the procedure after rebooting the EnSite X DWS was not possible, and the procedure could not be finished as planned. Further checking found that the field frame connections against the connector looked charred. There were no adverse patient consequences.

records.text: It was reported that the results in SCM (Soft Computer Middleware) are incorrect. The device was in clinical use. There was no report of patient or user harm. Analysis was performed by remote service personnel which included review of the customer complaint, review of available service documentation, remote review of the IBE server, and efforts to reproduce the reported issue. No error messages were identified, and the relevant messages had already been purged from the system prior to the investigation, preventing further analysis. Based on the results of the analysis, the product was confirmed to be operating per specifications and the cause of the reported problem could not be determined because the reported issue was not reproducible and the relevant system messages had already been purged before the investigation was initiated. The issue was resolved by remotely reviewing the IBE server, confirming that no diagnostic data remained available for analysis, and communicating the findings to the customer, who acknowledged the information. A review of the service history for this device shows no subsequent reports of the same issue following this service event, indicating that the problem has not recurred. An "internal error: reconnect to amplifier" message was observed when connecting the the EnSite X to the DWS with no transmission of ECG data. Surface and ECG patches were already placed on the patient when the error occurred. After rebooting the EnSite X amplifier and DWS, the error message "an amplifier hardware error has been detected. records.text: As reported, during a cardiac surgery using this HemoSphere Alta Monitor with the latest software version, connected to a Philips bedside monitor through the EC10/EC5 interface, incomplete transmission of physiological parameters was observed. Mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) was transmitted correctly; however, other expected parameters were not displayed on the Philips bedside monitor (see attached picture). Subsequent testing reproduced the issue, during which inaccurate Cardiac Index (CI) values were displayed on the Philips bedside monitor (see attached picture). Delayed transmission was also observed for other parameters when comparing values displayed on the HemoSphere Alta Monitor with those displayed on the Philips bedside monitor. Troubleshooting activities included replacement of the Ethernet cable, EC10 module, and EC5 module, and verification of the configuration settings; however, the reported issue persisted. Additional testing was performed using both HemoSphere and HemoSphere Alta interface configurations. Following the configuration change, blood temperature was displayed on the Philips bedside monitor under a configuration in which this parameter was not expected to be displayed, whereas it had not been displayed under the previous configuration. Differences in the availability of Cardiac Output and other advanced parameters were also observed between the tested configurations. There is no allegation of patient injury. The device was not available for evaluation. Primary Unique Device Identification (UDI) Number: (b)(4).The manufacturing records were reviewed for the lot involved and there is no indication of a related nonconformance. All process parameters were met and inspections passed successfully. Follow up is on going to clarify whether the device is available for evaluation. An investigation has been initiated to consider any potential factors that may have contributed to this complaint. A supplemental report will be sent with the evaluation results. records.text: It was reported that during a cardiac ablation procedure, approximately one hour into ablation, a catheter display/navigation lag was observed. The catheter intermittently partially disappeared from the display, became stuck at one displayed location, and later intermittently resumed normal movement. The display/navigation problems progressively worsened. Restarting the catheter interface unit did not resolve the issue. A workstation restart generated an internal graphics error that disappeared after an additional restart. Upon resuming the case, the catheter was not visible, and starting a new case did not restore visibility. Multiple restarts of the system and workstation and reconnection of the magnetic field generator did not resolve the issue. A new catheter was visible within the sheath; however, upon expansion in the atrium, it became stuck and no longer moved. Several attempts to restore catheter movement were unsuccessful, and an electroanatomical map could not be generated. The procedure was aborted mid-case and was not continued using another system. No patient complications have been reported as a result of this event. It was further reported the case was aborted under general anesthesia. During the EFO procedure a cancellation was noted when the EnSite X DWS was unable to communicate with the monitor. Troubleshooting was performed and the issue was initially resolved, however, during the study the EnSite X DWS shutdown and went black. Multiple attempts to restart, reboot and reconnect the DWS were unsuccessful. While troubleshooting, the previous DWS was reconnected and was able to start with no issues to confirm that the monitors and cables were functioning correctly. Dut to the upgrades on other systems they could not continue with this old DWS and reconnected the EnSite X DWS with successful startup. The previous study was resumed and working however, when attempting to close the study the EnSite X DWS shut down. A force restart was required and upon restarting the initial issue continued. While troubleshooting for approximately 2.5 hours, the patient was under anesthesia for approximately 2 hours of that total time. It was noted that the EnSite X DWS was experiencing issues prior to the start of the procedure, and it was decided to proceed with the procedure despite the issues. There were additional issues with the non-Abbott BARD system as well and no ablation could be performed and the procedure was cancelled.

records.reason_for_recall:
Boston Scientific has received reports indicating the grid mark overlay on the cross-sectional view did not present correctly when an OptiCross 18 Peripheral Imaging Catheter was connected to the AVVIGO+ Multi-Modality Guidance System while in either Live or Record mode. The Boston Scientific investigation determined that, due to a software anomaly, a 9-grid mark overlay is incorrectly displayed during Live mode when AVVIGO+ is connected to an OptiCross 18 Peripheral Imaging Catheter. Note that the correct overlay display for this catheter is the 15-grid mark overlay, which allows for a reference depth setting of 14.9mm for peripheral catheters.
This software anomaly is limited to Live or Record mode. In Review mode, the correct 15-grid mark overlay is displayed, and the vessel image is correctly scaled to the appropriate size.

The HemoSphere Advanced Monitor (HEM1) is intended to be used in combination with a compatible Edwards hemodynamic monitoring technology module and/or cable and accompanying Edwards accessories and/or disposables. LEDs within the oximetry cable transmit light fiber optically to the distal end of the catheter. The amount of light absorbed, refracted, and reflected depends on the relative amounts of oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin in the blood. This optical intensity data is gathered by the oximetry catheter, processed by the HemoSphere Oximetry Cable, and displayed on a compatible monitoring platform. Parameter output is mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) or central venous oxygen saturation (ScvO2).
